solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: French writer of Antigone adapted following Moliere’s lead (9)

indicators.note: an adapted text has been reworked, so its letters are rearranged
the anagram comes after Moliere's initial
a lead is what goes in front, so Moliere's first letter

annotation.surface: A theatre note: some French dramatist has adapted Antigone, taking his cue from Moliere.
annotation.walkthrough: Anouilh really did write an Antigone, so the surface sends you hunting for a playwright; the answer is instead the essayist, spelt out of the play's title.
annotation.definitionFit: Michel de Montaigne was the sixteenth-century French essayist.

entries.clue: Apricot sweet initially made exclusively by our shop (5)

indicators.note: take each following word's initial letter

blocks.note: initials of Made Exclusively By Our Shop

annotation.surface: A label boasting that the apricot confection on sale is a house speciality.
annotation.walkthrough: MEBOS is an obscure South African word, so the wordplay does all the work; trust the initials.
annotation.definitionFit: Mebos is a South African sweet of salted, sugared dried apricots.

entries.clue: Old PM on rural island, one of ours far from London? (15)

definitions.text: one of ours far from London?

blocks.note: country = rural, as in country life

annotation.surface: A former prime minister retires to some rural island, far from Westminster.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a northerner is one of 'our' countrymen, living far from the capital.
annotation.definitionFit: A north countryman is someone from the north of England, a long way from London.

entries.clue: Who questions a number being taken up on credit mostly (8)

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: one who questions

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top
most of the word, so drop its last letter

blocks.note: a number is a song in a show
TICK (credit, as in on tick) without its K

annotation.surface: Someone wonders about a figure being entered in the books, largely on credit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure in accounts; it is a song. 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
annotation.definitionFit: An agnostic questions whether God exists, neither believing nor denying.

entries.clue: Disused spot acquired to accommodate university (4)

indicators.note: the first word houses the next inside it

annotation.surface: An abandoned site has been bought to house a university campus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disused' tells you the sense of spot is archaic: a gout is an old word for a drop or splash, not the joint disease.
annotation.definitionFit: Gout in its old sense means a drop or spot, as in gouts of blood.

entries.clue: No one raised putting in blubber part, one in process of scrambling? (10)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word flips it to read upwards
the following letters go inside

annotation.surface: Nobody wants a piece of whale fat; someone is busy scrambling eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' reads as whale fat but is the verb, to weep. The question mark admits that scrambling a message is not scrambling an egg.
annotation.definitionFit: Encryption is the process of scrambling data so only the intended reader can decode it.

entries.clue: Course for royals held in Victoria’s cottage (5)

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: Some route for the royal family passes through Queen Victoria's cottage.
annotation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is the famous race meeting in Berkshire, founded by Queen Anne, which the royal family attends each June.
annotation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse closely associated with the royal family.

entries.clue: Italian place Mafia left in a mess (6)

indicators.note: a room in a mess has everything out of place, so the letters lose their order

annotation.surface: The Mafia abandoned some Italian town in chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the Mafia departing; it is just the letter L joining the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Amalfi is a town on Italy's southern coast.

entries.clue: Am monopolistic, sadly, about society and world view (15)

indicators.note: things gone sadly wrong are in disorder
the jumbled letters go around the next one

annotation.surface: A tycoon confesses, with regret, to cornering the market in society and in outlook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'World view' works both as a phrase meaning outlook and literally: a cosmopolitan sees the whole world as home.
annotation.definitionFit: Cosmopolitanism is the outlook of a citizen of the world, not bound to one nation.

entries.clue: Kentish Town school losing opening game (9)

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter

annotation.surface: A school in Kentish Town, the London district, forfeits its first match.
annotation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a district of north London, so the phrase looks like a place name; split it and it means a town in Kent. Tonbridge also has a famous school.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by splitting a London place name: read 'Kentish' as 'in Kent' and the phrase describes this market town in that county.

entries.clue: Noble artist and author lacking time for boastful adventurer (5,10)

indicators.note: the author's name goes without the letter for time

blocks.note: Edvard Munch, painter of The Scream

annotation.surface: An aristocratic painter and a writer, short of time, are set against a braggart.
annotation.walkthrough: The Baron's tall tales of his exploits made his name a byword for boastful exaggeration.
annotation.definitionFit: Baron Munchausen is the fictional teller of wildly exaggerated adventure stories.

entries.clue: Church is replacing sanctum’s interior division (6)

indicators.note: the new letters take the place of others
the inside letters of the word, the ones swapped out

blocks.note: SANCTUM with its interior ANCTU taken out; CH IS goes in its place

annotation.surface: A church is renovating the inner part of its sanctuary.
annotation.walkthrough: Apt on the surface too: a schism is a split in a church.
annotation.definitionFit: A schism is a division, especially within a church.

entries.clue: What might go into pumpernickel or dry bloomer, it’s said (8)

indicators.note: the words are to be heard, not read

annotation.surface: Ingredients in German black bread or in a dry loaf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' is a British loaf, so the surface stays in the bakery; here it is a flowering plant. Pumpernickel is a dark German rye bread.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: pumpernickel, a dark German loaf, is baked from coarse rye meal, so this is an ingredient that goes into it.

entries.clue: Take one flower as told, it’s yellow and in a jar (10)

definitions.text: it’s yellow and in a jar

indicators.note: as spoken, so read by ear

blocks.note: pick = take, a = one, lily = flower

annotation.surface: Instructions to choose a single bloom, with a note that it is yellow and kept in a vase.
annotation.walkthrough: The flower sets up a yellow lily in a vase; the jar holds a pickle instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a bright yellow mustard pickle of chopped vegetables, sold in jars.

entries.clue: Make well disposed pair tiptoe around (10)

indicators.note: the letters are turned around, rearranged

annotation.surface: Two people creep about on tiptoe, trying to keep someone sweet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a couple tiptoeing round a touchy person, which is roughly what propitiating means.
annotation.definitionFit: To propitiate is to win over or appease someone.

entries.clue: Buyer of a lot of neat alcohol right after a drink (9)

indicators.note: most of the word, not all of it

blocks.note: PURE (neat, undiluted) minus its last letter
a chaser is a shot taken straight after another drink

annotation.surface: Someone buying rounds of neat spirits with another drink straight after.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like R; it belongs to the cryptic description of a chaser, 'alcohol right after a drink'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the party who pays in a sale, the opposite of the vendor.

entries.clue: Reportedly out and proud? (4)

indicators.note: as reported by word of mouth, so by sound

blocks.note: in cricket a batsman bowled is out

annotation.surface: A rumour that someone has come out and is proud of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about coming out with pride; 'out' is cricket, where bowled means the ball hit the stumps and the batsman is dismissed.
annotation.definitionFit: Proud can mean standing out or brazen, as bold does.

entries.clue: Spot small dish (8)

blocks.note: a platter is a serving dish

annotation.surface: Someone notices a little plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as the verb see; it is the verb to fleck with drops.
annotation.definitionFit: Spot as a verb, to mark with drops: flicking paint over a wall leaves it spotted, and splattered.

entries.clue: Country’s head is late queen (4)

indicators.note: the first letter arrives late, moving to the end

blocks.note: the country; its head I goes to the back

annotation.surface: News that a nation's ruler, a queen, has died.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as dead; here it means arriving last, so IRAN becomes RANI.
annotation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife.

entries.clue: Partner about to return free ticket with story about cold (10)

indicators.note: the letters come back the other way
the story's word wraps round the next letter

blocks.note: a story is a lie, as in telling stories

annotation.surface: A partner is about to come back with a free ticket and a tale about a chill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' appears twice and does two different jobs: first as ca (circa), then as the instruction to wrap one piece round another.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrowed synonym: the answer means specifically a partner in wrongdoing, which the plain word 'partner' covers.

entries.clue: Worship always incorporated into religious teaching (6)

indicators.note: the first word is taken inside the next

blocks.note: RE = religious education, the school subject

annotation.surface: Constant worship built into the religion lessons.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a British school subject.
annotation.definitionFit: To revere is to worship or hold in deep respect.

entries.clue: Pegasus, say, and what it does for one it supports? (8)

annotation.surface: A puzzle about the winged horse of myth: what does it do, and what does it carry?
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the same horse: a horsefly is an insect that rides on horses, so the horse supports it.
annotation.definitionFit: A horsefly is a biting fly that settles on horses and other livestock.

entries.clue: Rumour king perhaps is entertaining a knight (6)

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in

blocks.note: a king is one kind of playing card
N is the knight in chess notation

annotation.surface: Gossip that the monarch is hosting a knight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King' suggests a monarch or chessman; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a card.
annotation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded rumour or false report.

entries.clue: Magistrates closely follow points (5)

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow at their heels
E and S, two compass points

annotation.surface: Officials keep a close eye on the details.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Points' is compass points, a crossword staple for N, S, E and W.
annotation.definitionFit: The doges were the chief magistrates of Venice and Genoa.

entries.clue: Past name for Stravinsky ballet (4)

annotation.surface: A former title of one of Stravinsky's ballets.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ballet that was renamed; the wordplay is just two parts put together.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is a named work, a 1957 piece choreographed by Balanchine, and the clue identifies it by its composer.

entries.clue: Total wizard coda to Schoenberg keeps Transfigured Night showing brilliance of Proms season (6,9)

indicators.note: a coda is the closing passage, so the last letter
the wizard holds the next letters inside
transfigured letters have changed form, so are rearranged

annotation.surface: A music critic hails a magical Schoenberg performance at the Proms.
annotation.walkthrough: Transfigured Night is a real Schoenberg piece, so the clue reads as a concert review; 'Transfigured' is the anagram indicator. The Proms are London's summer concert season.
annotation.definitionFit: Summer lightning is the flicker of distant lightning seen on summer nights, the season of the Proms.

entries.clue: Field of fruit — beginning to be harvested (5)

indicators.note: the first letter is cut away, as a crop is

annotation.surface: An orchard where the fruit is just starting to be picked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Field' reads as farmland; it is a field of study or expertise.
annotation.definitionFit: Field in the sense of scope or sphere: a wide field of interests is a wide range of them.

entries.clue: Symbol or a Greek letter that’s second to last? I don’t know (9)

definitions.note: the answer's Latin meaning, 'we do not know', standing for the person who says it

indicators.note: the S, for second, moves to the end

blocks.note: SIGN, a symbol, with its opening S sent to the end
standard abbreviation for second: the S taken from SIGN, now placed last

annotation.surface: A puzzled student asks whether a symbol or the penultimate Greek letter is meant, then gives up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second to last' looks like penultimate, the Greek letter psi; it means the S (second) moves to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Ignoramus is Latin for 'we do not know', and names someone who knows nothing.
